plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of a dark central disc surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, a behavior called heliotropism. It is widely grown as an ornamental and as an oilseed crop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide in places such as the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually a composite of up to 2,000 tiny individual florets, each of which can develop into a seed.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and attracts bees and butterflies in great numbers. It is grown for ornament, essential oils, and culinary use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Peak bloom from late June to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial whose large, showy flowers rise on tall stalks above round, water-repellent leaves. The blooms open in the morning and close at night over a few days. It is deeply symbolic in many Asian cultures and grows in ponds, lakes, and slow wetlands.
plants.location: Asia, from India and China to Japan and Vietnam, and northern Australia; widely cultivated in water gardens
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-textured surface that causes water and dirt to roll off, known as the 'lotus effect', which has inspired self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Eucalyptus caesia
plants.description: A small, weeping mallee-type eucalypt with powdery white-silver bark and branches. In late winter its large, pendulous, showy flowers appear and attract nectar-feeding birds. It is a rare species that is popular in gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter, roughly May to September in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southwestern Australia, restricted to granite outcrops near Wheatbelt region
plants.funFact: This species is naturally found on only a few granite outcrops in Western Australia, so it is considered rare in the wild.
